districts.name: Bengaluru Urban
districts.story: Bengaluru's darshinis serve filter coffee in a steel tumbler and dabarah, poured high to froth it: chicory-laced decoction, boiled milk and sugar.
districts.credit: "Indian filter coffee in Dabarah", Wikimedia Commons, CC BY-SA 3.0

districts.name: Bengaluru Rural
districts.story: Devanahalli's oval stone fort was rebuilt by Haider Ali in the 1700s, and Tipu Sultan was born in the town it guards.
districts.credit: "Remains of Devanahalli fort 02", Vaish, CC BY-SA 3.0

districts.name: Bengaluru South
districts.story: Channapatna's lacquered toys are turned from soft ivory-wood and coloured with vegetable dyes, a craft the town has kept for two centuries.
districts.credit: "Finished Channapatna toys", KartikMistry, CC BY-SA 4.0

districts.name: Chikkaballapur
districts.story: Nandi Hills rises 1,478 m above the plains; at dawn the valleys below fill with cloud, and Tipu Sultan once summered on its top.
districts.credit: "Sunrise at Nandi Hills", JzG, CC BY-SA 4.0

districts.name: Kolar
districts.story: The Kolar Gold Fields were among the deepest gold mines in the world, worked for over a century until they closed in 2001.
districts.credit: "Champion Reef Mine shaft", Adu65 at English Wikipedia, Public domain

districts.name: Tumakuru
districts.story: Tiptur's coconuts are prized across India for their thick, oil-rich kernels, dried into copra on farms around the town.
districts.credit: "Tiptur Coconut Plantation", unknown author, Public domain

districts.name: Chitradurga
districts.story: Chitradurga's seven-ringed stone fort winds over granite hills; Onake Obavva defended it with only a pestle.
districts.credit: "Chitradurga fort Image (10), Karnataka, India", Gpkp, CC BY-SA 4.0

districts.name: Davanagere
districts.story: Davanagere benne dosa is cooked crisp in a pool of white butter and served with a coconut chutney and potato palya.
districts.credit: "Davanagere Benne Dosa", Ravi Dwivedi, CC BY-SA 4.0

districts.name: Shivamogga
districts.story: At Jog Falls the Sharavathi river drops 253 m in four streams, Raja, Rani, Rover and Rocket, at their fullest in the monsoon.
districts.credit: "Jog Falls 05092016", Nikhilb239, CC BY 3.0

districts.name: Mysuru
districts.story: The sweet was first made in the Mysuru Palace kitchens for Krishnaraja Wadiyar IV: gram flour, ghee and sugar, cooked until it crumbles.
districts.credit: "Mysore Pak (2026)" by Gpkp, CC BY-SA 4.0

districts.name: Mandya
districts.story: Mandya's sugarcane fields feed the vats where cane juice is boiled down into golden blocks of jaggery, bella in Kannada.
districts.credit: "Harvesting Sugarcane Doddagowdana Koppalu Aug24 A7CR 02231", Timothy A. Gonsalves, CC BY-SA 4.0

districts.name: Chamarajanagar
districts.story: Bandipur's teak and bamboo forests are one of India's first tiger reserves, joined to Nagarhole and Mudumalai in a single wild corridor.
districts.credit: "Img tiger bandipur 01", Harish Garg, CC BY-SA 4.0

districts.name: Hassan
districts.story: At Belur and Halebidu the Hoysalas carved soapstone temples so finely that bracelets on the dancers' wrists still turn.
districts.credit: "Hoysaleswara Temple at Halebidu", Rohit Sharma, CC BY-SA 4.0

districts.name: Kodagu
districts.story: Kodagu's coffee grows in the shade of tall forest trees, with pepper vines climbing the trunks between the bushes.
districts.credit: "Ripe Seeds Coffee Robusta Coorg" by Timothy A. Gonsalves, CC BY-SA 4.0

districts.name: Chikkamagaluru
districts.story: Mullayanagiri is Karnataka's highest peak at 1,930 m, near the Baba Budangiri hills where coffee was first planted in India.
districts.credit: "Mullayanagiri peak", Anvesh1103, CC BY-SA 4.0

districts.name: Dakshina Kannada
districts.story: Mangalore buns are soft, sweet puris made with ripe banana in the dough, eaten for breakfast with coconut chutney.
districts.credit: "Mangalore buns in Udupi", Sohom Datta, CC0

districts.name: Udupi
districts.story: Udupi's temple kitchens gave the world its masala dosa: a thin rice crêpe folded around spiced potato.
districts.credit: "Masala dosa 01", Marajozkee, CC BY-SA 4.0

districts.name: Belagavi
districts.story: Belagavi kunda is milk slowly reduced with sugar until it caramelises into a rich, grainy brown sweet.
districts.credit: "Kunda mithai", Sanketghatnatti1274, CC BY-SA 4.0

districts.name: Bagalkot
districts.story: At Badami the Chalukyas cut four cave temples into red sandstone cliffs above the Agastya lake in the 6th century.
districts.credit: "A-cave-temple-at-badami", Rajeshodayanchal, CC BY-SA 3.0

districts.name: Vijayapura
districts.story: Gol Gumbaz, Mohammed Adil Shah's tomb, has one of the largest domes ever built; a whisper in its gallery echoes seven times.
districts.credit: "Gol Gumbaz-2020", Murali K, CC BY-SA 4.0

districts.name: Dharwad
districts.story: Dharwad peda is milk cooked down with sugar until it turns brown and grainy, a recipe a Thakur family brought here in the 1800s.
districts.credit: "Dharwad pedha", Maharana7573, CC BY-SA 4.0

districts.name: Gadag
districts.story: Lakkundi holds dozens of ornate Kalyani Chalukya temples and stepwells, carved in soft green-grey schist.
districts.credit: "Jain temple at Lakkundi built in the Kalyani Chalukya style", Dineshkannambadi at English Wikipedia, CC BY-SA 3.0

districts.name: Haveri
districts.story: Byadgi chillies are deep red and wrinkled, mild in heat but strong in colour; their market sets prices for all of India.
districts.credit: "Byadgi Chilli", Rajaramraok, CC BY-SA 4.0

districts.name: Uttara Kannada
districts.story: Gokarna is a temple town on the Arabian Sea, with Om beach curving below it in the shape of the sacred syllable.
districts.credit: "Paradise Beach, Gokarna", Sourabh.biswas003, CC BY-SA 4.0

districts.name: Kalaburagi
districts.story: Kalaburagi's Bahmani-era fort holds the Jama Masjid, roofed entirely with domes, while tur dal from its black soil feeds Karnataka.
districts.credit: "Gulbarga Fort Karnataka", Maverick on the move, CC BY-SA 4.0

districts.name: Bidar
districts.story: Bidriware is blackened zinc-copper alloy inlaid with pure silver, darkened with soil from inside Bidar's old fort.
districts.credit: "Bidriware vases and decanter", Randhirreddy at English Wikipedia, CC BY-SA 3.0

districts.name: Yadgir
districts.story: Yadgir's hill fort was built by the Yadavas of Devagiri and watches over the town from a granite outcrop.
districts.credit: "Yadgir Fort", Asim Rasool, CC BY-SA 4.0

districts.name: Raichur
districts.story: Raichur fort sits between the Krishna and Tungabhadra rivers, a prize fought over by the Vijayanagara and Bahmani kingdoms.
districts.credit: "Raichur Fort 1", Madhu B M, CC BY-SA 4.0

districts.name: Koppal
districts.story: Kinnal craftspeople carve light wood into toys, temple chariots and figures, then paint them in bright colours.
districts.credit: Karnataka tableau "Kinnal, an immortal colour craft", Republic Day 2013, Ministry of Defence, GODL-India

districts.name: Ballari
districts.story: Ballari's fort crowns a single granite hill, rebuilt by Hyder Ali with a French engineer in the 18th century.
districts.credit: "Bellary Fort in 2019", Ginevrajocosa88, CC BY-SA 4.0

districts.name: Vijayanagara
districts.story: Hampi's stone chariot stands before the Vittala temple, a shrine to Garuda carved to look as if its wheels could turn.
districts.credit: "Stone Chariot, Hampi 2", Ajayreddykalavalli, CC BY-SA 4.0
